title: POC Weekly Onboard: Staging Safety & Fallback Rehearsal
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + network diagram link
Run 95th pct latency bench with 2k QPS next Tue
Customer to validate SSO flow in staging and report failures
Schedule on-prem walkthrough for week of Jan 11
action_items: Maya Chen - Share SOC2 report and network diagram - 2027-01-07
Daniel Ruiz - Provision dedicated test key and sample load script - 2027-01-06
Ethan Cole - Confirm firewall rules for egress to Redwood hosted endpoints - 2027-01-08
Lina Gomez - Provide list of compliance controls required (GDPR & HIPAA) - 2027-01-10
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on staging safety checks, fallback playbook rehearsal, and access readiness. Key blockers: SSO token exchange failing intermittently, egress firewall rules, and needing SOC2 docs for procurement. Agreed next: security docs, latency bench, and on-prem walkthrough scheduling.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for hopping on, we wanted to run the staging safety and fallback rehearsal today, check access, and run through the playbook. how's everyone doing?
[00:15] Priya Patel: good, quick heads up we had an intermittent token exchange fail in staging this morning so that is the main thing on our side.
[00:32] Daniel Ruiz: ok when you say token exchange fail, is it the SAML assertion to the redwood control plane or the downstream host key negotiation? sometimes the assertion mapping trips on role mapping.
[00:48] Priya Patel: looks like the SAML assertion, the IdP returns a 200 but the mapping layer rejects it - we see a 403 in the session logs. Lina, you saw that right?
[00:56] Lina Gomez: yeah I captured the logs, i'll paste the snippet to the shared drive after this. it seems the nameid format gets munged, maybe our ADFS doing something odd. could be an attribute mapping miss.
[01:12] Maya Chen: ok understood. action item for us: i'll share the SSO test user and we'll reproduce. daniel can you attach the SSO debug guide?
[01:22] Daniel Ruiz: yep i'll upload the SAML debug checklist to the shared doc. link: https://redwood.app/pocs/mednova/sso-debug (note: internal link).
[01:32] Noah Rivers: one more thing - our firewall team still hasn't opened the egress to redwood-hosted endpoints for the staging subnet; we have a change window tomorrow but wanted to confirm required IP ranges.
[01:45] Maya Chen: we sent a network diagram in onboarding email but i'll resend the minimal egress ranges. also if you prefer private deployment we can schedule an on-prem walkthrough.
[01:55] Priya Patel: budget favors hosted for now but we need assurances on fallback: if hosted capacity is constrained can we fail to a smaller quantized model in the dedicated pool or to a lower-latency region?
[02:12] Daniel Ruiz: yes that's part of the platform. recommended pattern: primary route to hosted xlarge -> fallback to hosted quantized medium -> fallback to dedicated pool or region. There is a routing policy config. note though, fallback ordering affects average latency and cost.
[02:30] Ethan Cole: can you talk numbers? our SLA target is p95 < 150ms for short prompts (<256 tokens). is that realistic with batching?
[02:40] Daniel Ruiz: so for <256 tokens and minimal batching p95 of 120-160ms is feasible on our verified profiles for the model family you picked, but at 2k QPS you'll want autoscale and smart batching. with continuous batching the per-token cost goes down but latency will typically be around 140-220ms depending on load.
[03:02] Priya Patel: our primary objection is cost vs latency - procurement wants cost predictability. can Redwood provide a simple unit cost estimate for the two routing scenarios?
[03:14] Maya Chen: yes we'll produce a cost matrix: hosted only vs hosted+dedicated with observed bench numbers. we'll include expected token costs and a 99th/95th latency estimate.
[03:26] Lina Gomez: security checklist - we need KMS integration details, audit logs retention policy, and whether keys can be customer-managed HSM.
[03:36] Tom Harper: we support customer-managed keys via KMIP/HSM integrations in private deployment and with hosted we integrate commonly with AWS KMS using envelope encryption. audit logs are shipped to your SIEM with configurable retention. i'll share the compliance pack.
[03:51] Priya Patel: does Redwood store PII in logs? procurement flagged that.
[03:58] Tom Harper: default logs redact prompt text by policy unless you opt-in for full logging for evals. for HIPAA/PHI we recommend private or dedicated with specific retention settings.
[04:12] Ethan Cole: about the rehearsal - we wanted to simulate a regional outage and confirm the fallback triggers. is there an automated failover playbook we can step through?
[04:22] Daniel Ruiz: yes, we can trigger a canary failover in the routing layer. we'll do a dry-run: step 1 set region A weight to zero, step 2 confirm service fallback to region B, step 3 confirm graceful degradation to quantized model. do you want to do that now or schedule?
[04:40] Priya Patel: let's schedule it after we get SSO and firewall sorted, prefer a controlled dry-run with SRE present.
[04:50] Maya Chen: fair. next steps: we'll run a scheduled rehearsal once Ethan confirms firewall and Priya confirms SSO.
[04:58] Noah Rivers: for the latency bench - what's the recommended harness? we use locust internally, can we run a Redwood-provided script?
[05:06] Daniel Ruiz: yes we'll provide a python harness and a k6 script. Daniel: i'll attach the script to the repo and also include a sample token rotation script for long-running tests.
[05:18] Priya Patel: when you say quantized model fallback, is that a different model family or the same weights with INT8? our QA worries about hallucinations increasing.
[05:29] Daniel Ruiz: it's the same base model compiled with quantization-friendly kernels (INT8 per-layer). qualitatively outputs are very similar for many tasks but we will run your eval prompts through the quantized profile and show side-by-side diffs during the bench.
[05:44] Lina Gomez: please add evaluation metrics we care about to the bench: exact match, BLEU for our doc extraction task, and hallucination rate threshold.
[05:57] Maya Chen: noted. i'll add those as part of the bench runbook.
[06:05] Priya Patel: procurement also asked for a copy of SOC2 and penetration test summary before we sign the trial amendment.
[06:12] Maya Chen: I'll share SOC2 and recent pen test summary by Friday. (short pause)
[06:20] Ethan Cole: quick clarifying question on observability: can we expose token-level latency per-route in the console and get traces for individual requests?
[06:31] Tom Harper: yes console has per-route token breakdown and tracing hooks; we stream traces to your tracing endpoint and we can set token-level cost tags.
[06:41] Noah Rivers: if we stream traces, is PII removed?
[06:45] Tom Harper: yes we support redaction; default settings remove sensitive fields but you can configure for more detailed traces in a secure vault.
[06:55] Maya Chen: ok let's recap real quick.
[07:00] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood to share SOC2+network diagram and SAML debug guide (Maya/Daniel), 2) Daniel to provision test key and bench harness, 3) MedNova to open egress to redwood ranges and confirm SSO test user (Ethan/Priya), 4) schedule a controlled failover rehearsal once access and firewall are green.
[07:22] Priya Patel: that sounds right. can you also include an estimated cost delta for enabling a dedicated pool vs hosted only? procurement wants a 3-month projection.
[07:31] Maya Chen: yes cost delta included in the follow-up.
[07:35] Lina Gomez: adding a security note - we'll want the audit log retention extended to 1 year for the pilot environment.
[07:42] Tom Harper: we can configure that in the retention policy.
[07:46] Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[07:50] Ethan Cole: none from me.
[07:52] Noah Rivers: all good.
[07:54] Maya Chen: thanks everyone we'll send the follow-up with links and next steps by tomorrow. meeting adjourned.
